correctness.rationale: The greedy residual-ratio elimination assigns levels nondecreasingly and satisfies each exact target, proving surjectivity for all finite graphs and nonnegative targets. For two profiles every min-edge change is a convex mixture of endpoint changes. Symmetric weights give one unit of strict column diagonal dominance, so the reverse triangle inequality summed over coordinates yields the global sharp l1 expansion and injectivity. For capped-linear benefit with r_i>c_i>0, each best response is the unique own collection reaching its saturation threshold, so Nash profiles equal inverse images of threshold vectors. An explicit high-level vertex attains inverse constant one on every graph; exact tests support the proof. Finite tests alone are not offered as universal proof.

value.rationale: The primary 2026 reciprocal data-exchange model highlights loss of order-theoretic structure in graph-restricted sharing. The new exact dimension- and degree-free inverse one-norm stability bound provides network-wide robustness to heterogeneous target shocks and ensures a unique prediction for a natural capped-value class. Its sharpness is substantive: even connected stars produce unbounded infinity-norm inverse amplification, showing total-adjustment geometry is essential rather than a generic linear estimate.
